title: The Recipe of Lake Minnow
premise: In the lakeside town of Minnow, seventeen-year-old Paloma Blackwood bakes her grief into bread — loaves that taste like the mother she lost five years ago, when a boating accident took her and left Paloma too afraid to want anything. When her history teacher pairs her with Theo Vance, the boy whose family's marina was blamed for the accident, for a semester project on local memory, their reluctant research unearths a truth neither family wants: the accident was no one's fault but everyone's silence. As Paloma and Theo fall into something fragile and real, she must enter the county baking championship to save her father's failing bakery — and then risk everything by baking the truth of what really happened into one final loaf, read aloud at prom, so the whole town can finally grieve together.
about_author: Freya Sandoval grew up in a small lake town where every diner claimed the same pie recipe and nobody talked about the summer the water took two boats. She writes stories about stubborn kids, inherited silences, and the food that holds families together. This is her second novel.

chapters.title: The Bread That Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She opens the bakery before dawn, kneading a loaf that tastes exactly like her mother's cardamom bread — the only recipe she can still make without crying. Establishes her rule: bake feelings in, never say them out loud. Emotional beat: careful loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Mr. Okafor announces semester projects on 'the town's living memory' and pairs her with Theo Vance. The classroom goes silent; everyone knows about the accident and the blame. They agree to do the minimum, separately. Beat: dread sharpened into hostility.

chapters.title: Flour on His Sleeves
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He shows up at the bakery because his half of the project is oral histories and the bakery is where old-timers talk. Paloma tries to throw him out; her father hires him instead. Beat: grudging proximity, first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: What the Lake Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First interview: Mrs. Ibarra, who saw both boats that night, starts a sentence about the fog and stops herself. Paloma realizes Theo has spent five years apologizing for a crime he didn't commit. Beat: uneasy recognition of a fellow survivor.

chapters.title: The Championship Flyer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The bank calls about the bakery loan; her father hides the notice. The county baking championship's prize would clear the debt. She signs up before she can think. Beat: fear converted into desperate ambition.

chapters.title: Practice Runs and Bad Faith
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He becomes her unofficial taste-tester since he's at the bakery anyway; their arguments over recipes turn into real conversation. He admits he doesn't remember his sister's face anymore. Beat: intimacy arriving sideways, through flour and sugar.

chapters.title: The Missing Logbook
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Project research hits a wall: the marina's weather logbook from the night of the accident is missing from the town archive. Someone checked it out years ago and never returned it. Beat: mystery ignites; suspicion lands close to home.

chapters.title: Prom Is a Battlefield
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. School politics intrude: championship finals are scheduled the same week as prom, and Theo's ex-friend Dana spreads rumors that Paloma is using him. A near-kiss interrupted. Beat: social pressure tightening around the growing bond.

chapters.title: My Father's Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She confronts her dad about the loan and the logbook — and learns he was the last person to check it out, trying to prove the Vances' boat had faulty lights. He never finished reading it. Beat: betrayal; the enemy was inside the house all along.

chapters.title: Sourdough and Standoffs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds out about the logbook from Dana and confronts Paloma mid-championship-practice. She can't defend her father without destroying him. He walks out. Beat: the relationship fractures on the fault line of their families.

chapters.title: Regional Round
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She competes alone, hollow, and barely advances with technically perfect, emotionally dead bread. The judge's comment: 'Nothing at stake here.' Beat: rock bottom — perfection as another form of hiding.

chapters.title: The Fog Statement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Going through his late grandfather's things, Theo finds the actual missing logbook — his grandfather took it to protect the marina, and it proves BOTH boats ran dark in an unforecast squall. No villain. Just weather and luck. Beat: truth as burden rather than weapon.

chapters.title: Halfway Point: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo brings the logbook to Paloma, not to the newspaper. They read it together through the night, grieving side by side for the first time. They decide the project — and the truth — belongs to the whole town. Beat: alliance rebuilt on honesty.

chapters.title: Recipe Reconstruction
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She begins designing the championship bake: a bread based on her mother's recipe but finished with lake-salt caramel — the taste of that night. Her father sees the sketch and finally tells her his own version of the accident. Beat: intergenerational grief surfacing.

chapters.title: Dana's Leverage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Dana discovers the logbook exists and threatens to release it framed to reignite the feud unless Theo drops the project. Theo refuses. Beat: stakes externalized; the truth now has enemies with deadlines.

chapters.title: The Bake That Broke
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Championship semifinal disaster: the oven fails, her signature loaf collapses, and she freezes in front of the crowd — until Theo steps up beside her and they rebuild it from scraps in forty minutes. They advance. Beat: partnership proven under fire.

chapters.title: Leaked
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dana releases a doctored excerpt of the logbook online; the town erupts, the Vances' marina is vandalized, and Paloma's father is named as the original thief. Both families under siege. Beat: consequences arrive; the cost of survival made visible.

chapters.title: Prom Eve
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the eve of everything — finals, prom, publication of the full truth — Paloma and Theo admit they love each other, quietly, in the closed bakery. She decides the final bake will be the full story, served at prom, with the complete logbook printed alongside. Beat: resolve crystallizing into courage.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Finals day. She bakes the lake-salt loaf flawlessly — and wins, but the victory feels small against what tomorrow requires. Her father, watching, weeps openly for the first time in five years. Beat: triumph revealed as rehearsal.

chapters.title: The Loaf at Prom
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At prom, instead of a speech, Paloma serves the bread and reads the logbook aloud — the fog, the failed radio, both boats running dark. Theo stands beside her. The gym goes quiet, then Mrs. Ibarra finishes the sentence she started months ago. Beat: climax — public truth, communal grief, love declared without words.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Fallout and grace: the town doesn't heal overnight, but the feud dissolves into shared mourning; a memorial is planned for the lake. Paloma's father and Theo's mother co-sign the bakery's new lease. Beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Recipe of Lake Minnow
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. One year later: the bakery renamed, a new memorial bread sold every June with proceeds for the lighthouse fund. Paloma writes the final recipe card — ingredients listed as memory, salt, courage — and pins it above the counter. Beat: resolution; survival's price paid, its sweetness kept.
